name: Cemetery Founding
description: A group of civic and church leaders established the cemetery so that community members could be buried with dignity and respect, free from the neglected conditions of existing burial grounds.

name: Civil Unrest of 1906
description: A period of violent unrest that swept through the area over several days. Businesses and homes were destroyed and residents were attacked. The event reshaped the community's geography and deepened solidarity.

name: Voter Registration Drives
description: Sustained campaigns to register Black voters in the county. Led by civic leaders, these drives transformed the local political landscape and helped elect more representative officials.

name: Community Insurance Co. Founded
description: A local entrepreneur purchased a failing mutual aid association and built it into a major insurance company, which became one of the largest Black-owned businesses in the region.

name: Commercial District Golden Era
description: The main commercial avenue became a thriving center of Black-owned businesses, churches, newspapers, and cultural institutions that anchored the African American community.

name: Workers' Labor Movement
description: Workers organized across trades — porters, domestic workers, garment workers — demanding fair wages and safer conditions. These labor efforts connected to broader national movements for economic justice.
